chunks: 540 - It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim that he said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Do we visit the dead? He said, “Yes.” I said: Do they know of us when we come to them? He said, “Yes, by Allah, they surely know of you, rejoice in you, and find comfort in you.”

He said: I said: Then what should we say when we come to them? He said, “Say: O Allah, draw the earth away from their sides, raise their spirits to You, grant them from Yourself pleasure, and cause to dwell with them from Your mercy that by which You join their loneliness and comfort their desolation.”
“Indeed, You are Powerful over all things.”

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening vocative of supplication
key_terms.الْمَوْتَىٰ: the deceased; those who have died
key_terms.رَحْمَتِكَ: Your mercy; Allah’s mercy bestowed upon them
key_terms.رِضْوَانًا: good pleasure; divine acceptance and favor
key_terms.لَيَعْلَمُونَ: they surely know; indicating awareness of the visitors
key_terms.وَحْشَتَهُمْ: their desolation; the loneliness and estrangement of the grave
key_terms.وَيَفْرَحُونَ: they rejoice; expressing their happiness at the visit

ai.seo_question: Do the dead know when we visit their graves, and what du'a should be recited for them?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the deceased are aware of the visits of the living, rejoice in them, and find comfort through them. It also transmits a supplication to be recited at graves, asking Allah to show mercy to the dead, relieve their loneliness, and grant them His good pleasure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.540 - It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim that He said:

"I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as): Do the dead know when we visit them?"
Imam (as) said: “Yes, by Allah (swt), they know of your visits and they rejoice and find comfort in your presence”

I said: "What should we say when we visit them?"
Imam (as) said: Say;
Allahumma jāfi al-arda ‘an junūbihim, wa ṣā‘id ilayka arwāḥahum, wa laqqihim minka riḍwānan, wa askin ilayhim min raḥmatika mā taṣilu bihi waḥdatahum wa tu’nisu bihi waḥshatahum, innaka ‘alā kulli shay’in qadīr.
"O’ Allah (swt), make the earth light upon their sides, raise their souls to You, grant them Your pleasure, and send upon them from Your mercy that which connects their loneliness and soothes their desolation.
Truly, You are powerful over all things."
